name: Henry Clifton Sorby
summary: British mineralogist who founded microscopical petrography and applied optical methods to rock analysis.

name: Brewster
summary: British mineralogist and pioneer in demonstrating mineral structure via light action.

name: Rev. Walter Mitchell
summary: Mathematical tutor and author of a treatise on Crystallography in Orr's 'Circle of the Sciences'.

name: William Crawford Williamson
summary: Friend who taught Sorby the art of making thin sections of hard materials.

name: David Forbes
summary: Friend and disciple of Sorby who studied rocks by Sorby's method.

name: Zirkel
summary: German scientific worker who became conspicuous among Sorby's friends and disciples.

name: Renard
summary: Worker who took up Sorby's method alongside Zirkel and David Forbes.

name: Julien
summary: Stylist of crystal cavities as 'sealed flasks of crystals'.

name: Mrs. M. E. Waller
summary: Painter of the portrait presented to Dr. Sorby in 1906.

name: Sheffield
summary: Native town where Sorby spent much of his life and conducted work.

name: Yorkshire coast
summary: Location of the calcareous grit Sorby analyzed in 1850.

name: Sheffield Museum
summary: Museum to which Sorby left experimental specimens by his will.

name: Geological Society
summary: Scientific society where Sorby presented memoirs and served as president.

name: Royal Microscopical Society
summary: Society over which Sorby presided from 1875 to 1877.

name: Sheffield Literary and Philosophical Society
summary: Sheffield institution Sorby supported and had fifty years of connexion with.

name: Firth College
summary: College in whose foundation Sorby was the leading spirit.

name: University of Sheffield
summary: University evolved from Firth College, to which Sorby left part of his fortune.

name: Mineralogical Magazine
summary: Journal publishing this obituary and Sorby's 1877 obituary of Forbes.

name: The Naturalist
summary: Journal where Sorby's portrait first appeared in 1906.

name: Glimpse
summary: Yacht bought by Sorby in 1875 for research and travel.

name: Orr's 'Circle of the Sciences'
summary: Publication containing Mitchell's treatise on Crystallography.

name: Essays on the Endowment of Research
summary: Volume containing Sorby's 1876 essay 'Unencumbered Research; a Personal Experience'.

name: Geological Magazine
summary: Magazine where J.W.J. wrote about the origin of microscopic petrography in 1908.
